The father who shields his son from suffering

chapter_summary: A prince is born to the Shakya clan, and the wise men prophesy he will be either a great king or a great sage. His father, fearing the prophecy, builds a palace of pleasure to shield him from suffering, but a restlessness grows in the prince — a question the palace cannot answer. When he rides beyond the walls, he sees four sights that shatter his world: an old man, a sick man, a corpse, and a wandering ascetic serene and at peace. For the first time he sees that all beings are subject to age, sickness, and death — and that there might be a way beyond them. The question takes hold of him and will not let go: why do we suffer, and can suffering be ended?
